Use `GET /v3/accounts` with a `filters` query parameter scoped to the identity's ID. The `filters` field supports the standard ISC filter syntax, and `identityId` is the field to target.

## Request

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts?filters=identityId%20eq%20%22{identityId}%22
Authorization: Bearer {token}
```

## Example with curl

```bash
IDENTITY_ID="2c9180835d2e5168015d32f890ca1581"
TENANT="your-org"
TOKEN="eyJ..."

curl -X GET \
  "https://${TENANT}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts?filters=identityId%20eq%20%22${IDENTITY_ID}%22&count=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

## Example with Python (requests)

```python
import requests

tenant = "your-org"
token = "eyJ..."
identity_id = "2c9180835d2e5168015d32f890ca1581"

response = requests.get(
    f"https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
    params={
        "filters": f'identityId eq "{identity_id}"',
        "count": True,       # returns X-Total-Count header
        "limit": 250,        # max page size
    }
)

response.raise_for_status()
accounts = response.json()

print(f"Total accounts: {response.headers.get('X-Total-Count')}")
for acct in accounts:
    print(f"  [{acct['sourceName']}] {acct['name']}  (id: {acct['id']})")
```

## Key notes

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Filter field | `identityId eq "{id}"` |
| Pagination | Use `limit` + `offset`; set `count=true` to get `X-Total-Count` header |
| Required scope | `idn:accounts:read` (or `idn:accounts:manage`) |
| Required user level | `ORG_ADMIN`, `SOURCE_ADMIN`, `SOURCE_SUBADMIN`, or `HELPDESK` |

Each returned account object includes `sourceName`, `sourceId`, `name`, `nativeIdentity`, and the full attribute map — giving you a complete picture of that identity across every connected source.
